# Browser Journey QA Analyst

This skill gives one Crew the Browser Journey QA Analyst capability. It can seed a new Crew or be added to a compatible Crew without replacing its identity. Use the customer’s approved test and release systems.

## Setup through chat

Read templates/browser-journey-qa-analyst/TEMPLATE_SETUP.json and templates/browser-journey-qa-analyst/SETUP.md. Verify each check with the customer’s real build, policy, and evidence before adding its ID to completed_steps. Preserve prior progress; report verified, blocked, and next. Chat-only and manual-only are valid optional decisions.

## First useful result

1. Confirm the journey revision, expected outcome, exact build, environment, account, test-data bounds, and recording policy before execution.
2. Reuse a verified browser profile and canonical locators. Record each attempt with start time, result, screenshots or video, console/network evidence status, and source revision.
3. Distinguish product failure, test failure, environment blocker, and unresolved evidence. A retry is a separate attempt and never erases the first failure.
4. Return reproduction steps, likely owner, missing evidence, and the review needed before changing a test or product.
5. Retest the same approved journey against a named later build and report both observations.

Deliver **An attempt-level journey result with exact build and environment, pass/fail or blocked status, reproduction steps, and linked visual and console/network evidence.** A pass requires all required assertions and evidence; skipped, blocked, missing, or stale attempts remain visible and cannot become a pass.

## Source probe and acceptance

Run one approved journey against a pinned build and environment using an authorized test account. Save the attempt ID, required assertion results, recording and console/network artifact IDs, and one failed or blocked step. A successful retry must remain a separate attempt.

Reproduce one observed failure from the saved attempt on the same build, or mark it unresolved with the missing evidence. Check that a skipped assertion, absent required recording, or blocked account cannot yield pass.

## Follow-through

On a later run, retain earlier attempts, compare the same journey and build identity rule, and record changed test or environment revisions before claiming a regression was fixed.

## Fictional worked example

Fictional input: journey=signup-to-project@v3; build=sha:abc123; environment=preview-17; expected=new user creates a project; account=test-user-17; required evidence=video and console/network log.

Fictional output: attempt=qa-17-01; journey=signup-to-project@v3; build=sha:abc123; environment=preview-17; observed=project creation returned HTTP 403 after signup; verdict=fail; video=asset:qa-17-01.mp4; console/network=asset:qa-17-01.json; reproduction=sign in as test-user-17, submit project form, observe 403; owner=project-api-owner; retest=pending.

Inadequate: “Signup failed; retry later.” Reason: It omits the tested build, expected step, attempt, evidence, reproducible failure, and owner.

## Workflow Playbook and handoff

The Critical Journey Validation Workflow can consume a journey-result/v1 record keyed by journey revision, build, environment, attempt ID, observed outcome, evidence links, classification, and owner. A release gate must verify exact build identity and required suite completeness. The existing Workflow Playbook is browser-qa/critical-journey-validation. Builder must bind the exact output path and schema before another Crew consumes a result. Confirm source truth and customer policy independently.

## Boundaries

Do not change production data, weaken assertions, approve a release, or create a ticket or message without the authorized action route and owner review. Installing this skill enables no schedule, trigger, function, Automation, notification, or write. Do not copy another Crew’s credentials.

# Flaky Test Investigator

This skill gives one Crew the Flaky Test Investigator capability. It can seed a new Crew or be added to a compatible Crew without replacing its identity. Use the customer’s approved test and release systems.

## Setup through chat

Read templates/flaky-test-investigator/TEMPLATE_SETUP.json and templates/flaky-test-investigator/SETUP.md. Verify each check with the customer’s real build, policy, and evidence before adding its ID to completed_steps. Preserve prior progress; report verified, blocked, and next. Chat-only and manual-only are valid optional decisions.

## First useful result

1. Bind one canonical test, source revision, build, browser profile, environment, fixtures, and approved expectation.
2. Compare original and repeated isolated attempts with consistent inputs; retain both passing and failing traces and timestamps.
3. Check order dependence, shared state, network conditions, product races, locator drift, and environment outages; label the cause unresolved when evidence is insufficient.
4. Propose a bounded experiment and exact candidate fix with owner, risk, and verification criterion. Preserve original assertions.
5. After any approved change, rerun the canonical test under the agreed stability policy and keep its earlier failures visible.

Deliver **An attempt-by-attempt flake investigation with controlled inputs, failure and pass evidence, cause hypotheses, and a reviewable stabilization proposal.** A green retry is not proof of stability; report attempt count, result distribution, environment and build identity, and confidence limits.

## Source probe and acceptance

Fetch the canonical test revision and at least one original failed attempt plus its retry for the same build, environment, browser profile, and fixtures. Save each CI run and trace ID; a green summary without the original failure is insufficient.

Run or inspect a bounded set of isolated attempts under fixed inputs, retain the result distribution, and classify product, test, environment, or unresolved. Reject a proposed wait, quarantine, or assertion change when the cause is still unresolved.

## Follow-through

Use the same test and build keys to compare new attempts; reopen a prior classification when product or environment evidence contradicts it.

## Fictional worked example

Fictional input: test=login-refresh@v4; build=sha:def456; environment=staging-eu; fixtures=account-22; allowed attempts=5 isolated; prior result=pass after CI retry.

Fictional output: attempts=flake-22-01..05 on sha:def456/staging-eu with same fixtures; results=fail, pass, fail, pass, fail; failing traces show refresh token response delayed after assertion; classification=unresolved product-or-environment race; confidence=low; owner=auth-team; proposal=inspect token service timing before any test change; original assertions retained.

Inadequate: “It passed on retry, so increase the wait and mark green.” Reason: A retry does not establish a test defect; this hides product and environment evidence and changes the assertion policy without review.

## Workflow Playbook and handoff

The Flaky-Test Detection and Stabilization Workflow can consume flake-investigation/v1 with stable test and build IDs, attempt IDs, evidence, classification, confidence, candidate change, approval state, and later stability check. The existing Workflow Playbook is browser-qa/flaky-test-detection-stabilization. Builder must bind the exact output path and schema before another Crew consumes a result. Confirm source truth and customer policy independently.

## Boundaries

Do not silently quarantine or skip a test, weaken an assertion, inflate waits, or change canonical test source without owner review and an authorized route. Installing this skill enables no schedule, trigger, function, Automation, notification, or write. Do not copy another Crew’s credentials.

# Release Quality Assistant

This skill gives one Crew the Release Quality Assistant capability. It can seed a new Crew or be added to a compatible Crew without replacing its identity. Use the customer’s approved test and release systems.

## Setup through chat

Read templates/release-quality-assistant/TEMPLATE_SETUP.json and templates/release-quality-assistant/SETUP.md. Verify each check with the customer’s real build, policy, and evidence before adding its ID to completed_steps. Preserve prior progress; report verified, blocked, and next. Chat-only and manual-only are valid optional decisions.

## First useful result

1. Bind the requested release, commit SHA, build artifact, deployment environment, policy revision, and cutoff time.
2. Enumerate every required suite and group from policy before reading results; join results only by exact tested identity.
3. Treat missing, cancelled, stale, skipped, blocked, or mismatched results as nonpassing. Preserve distinct rerun attempts.
4. Derive pass, fail, or needs-review from the configured rule and show evidence and owner decisions for every exception.
5. Publish a status only through an authorized route and retain the provider receipt; a proposed or attempted status is not a published gate.

Deliver **A release quality brief with exact commit/build and environment, required suite matrix, missing or stale evidence, and proposed pass, fail, or needs-review decision.** A green CI summary alone does not prove the required suites ran against the reviewed build. Show policy, tested identity, source IDs, and receipt.

## Source probe and acceptance

Read the release policy revision and enumerate its required suites before fetching CI results. Join each run to the exact commit, build artifact, environment, suite revision, and cutoff; include a missing or mismatched result in the review.

Recompute the gate verdict from the complete required-suite matrix. Prove that a green CI summary with a missing suite, stale result, different SHA, or unresolved waiver remains nonpassing; record the release owner decision separately from any published status.

## Follow-through

Re-evaluate each new build independently; retain prior failures and waivers, and never reuse a passing result from a different SHA or environment.

## Fictional worked example

Fictional input: release=rc-28; SHA=987fed; build=artifact:rc-28-987fed; environment=preview-28; policy=gate-v5 requiring auth and critical-journey suites; owner=release-lead.

Fictional output: release=rc-28; SHA=987fed; build=artifact:rc-28-987fed; environment=preview-28; policy=gate-v5; auth=pass run:auth-19 on same build; critical-journey=missing; verdict=needs_review; owner=release-lead; published_status=none; next=run required journey suite on exact artifact.

Inadequate: “CI is green; release approved.” Reason: It does not bind the reviewed artifact or account for the missing required journey suite and lacks an owner decision or delivery receipt.

## Workflow Playbook and handoff

The Release and PR Quality Gate Workflow can consume release-quality-brief/v1 with release, SHA, build, environment, policy revision, required-suite matrix, verdict, reviewer, and delivery receipt. Engineering may consume a separate blocker ledger for fixes. The existing Workflow Playbook is browser-qa/release-pr-quality-gate. Builder must bind the exact output path and schema before another Crew consumes a result. Confirm source truth and customer policy independently.

## Boundaries

Do not merge, deploy, waive a required suite, auto-approve needs-review, or post an external status without the release owner and authorized action route. Installing this skill enables no schedule, trigger, function, Automation, notification, or write. Do not copy another Crew’s credentials.
